name: meeple-loop-no-starting-meeples-v1
description: THE BOOTSTRAP CONTROL for the meeple loop. The design hands every player one meeple of EACH of the five colours at setup, not drawn from the island bag, so a seat can visit any open door from turn one. This arm starts every supply EMPTY and asks what that gift is actually paying for. IT IS A REAL QUESTION AND NOT A TIDY-UP, because the starting five are the entire reason the loop can turn at all in the opening: with no meeples in supply the only legal bonus is Collect on an empty board, which is a bare Draw 1, and the first meeple anyone can spend has to arrive from an island delivery - which needs a barn, which needs a harvest, which needs several turns of building. THE PREDICTION. An empty start should push the whole visit economy several rounds later, flatten the hook badly in the first third, and make the opening indistinguishable from the v31 game it is meant to replace. If it does NOT - if the hook recovers to near the shipped arm's figure - then the starting five are pure acceleration rather than the engine's ignition, and the component count question in the handoff (5 per player plus 1 per tile is 32 at four seats against a bag of 25) gets much easier, because the bag stops needing to grow. READ IN THIS ORDER: (1) the hook by game third, not just the whole-game figure, because this arm's whole effect is a delay and a single average will hide it; (2) the bonus mix, watching the empty-board collect share in the first third, which is the solitaire opening this arm risks creating; (3) game length, because a loop that starts late is a longer game; (4) deliveries per player, since island meeples are now the ONLY source and the delivery rate and the visit rate become the same curve. TREAT A GOOD RESULT HERE WITH SUSPICION: the bots are self-regarding and price a meeple given to a rival at zero, so they will underweight exactly the circulation this arm removes. ⚠️ STATUS, 04/09/2026: the meeple loop is now the shipped default, so the visitCurrency line in this overlay's `set` is redundant and is kept only to say what the arm is a variant of. startingMeeplesPerColour 0 is still a live variant, and the answer it gave is now part of the shipped design's justification rather than an open question: the hook collapsed to 0.09 and the empty-board collect took 87% of turns, so the starting five are the loop's ignition and the bag has to grow to carry them.
